summary: This note is a long Wikipedia-derived overview of the Qing dynasty (1644–1912), China's last imperial dynasty. It covers the founding and Manchu military organization (Eight Banners, Green Standard Army), the conquest of Ming China and the role of Wu Sangui and Han defectors, the consolidation of legitimacy through bureaucracy and Central Asian ties, and the Cixi-era court politics. It also describes the dynasty's loss of peripheral territories, the Boxer crisis, the 1911 revolution and the 1912 abdication, plus later events such as Manchukuo and Qing trade restrictions.
one_line: Overview of the Qing dynasty, China's last imperial dynasty (1644–1912), covering its founding, military, court politics, territorial losses and collapse.
key_facts: The Qing dynasty ruled China from 1644 to 1912, with a brief abortive restoration in 1917, and was preceded by the Ming dynasty and succeeded by the Republic of China.
Nurhaci declared himself the "Bright Khan" of the Later Jin state, and his son Hong Taiji renamed the dynasty Great Qing in 1636.
Li Zicheng's rebel forces were defeated in battle by Wu Sangui and Dorgon on May 27, 1644.
The Guangxu Emperor died on November 14, 1908, and Empress Dowager Cixi died on November 15, 1908.
An autopsy conducted nearly a century later confirmed lethal levels of arsenic in the Guangxu Emperor's corpse.
Puyi was appointed successor at the age of two, leaving Zaifeng with the regency.
The Wuchang Uprising of October 10, 1911, led to the creation of the Republic of China in Nanjing with Sun Yat-sen as provisional head.
On 12 February 1912, Longyu issued an imperial edict bringing about the abdication of the child emperor Puyi, ending over 2,000 years of Imperial China.
In 1900, Boxers murdered foreign missionaries and large numbers of Chinese Christians, then converged on Beijing to besiege the Foreign Legation Quarter.
The Eight-Nation Alliance entered China and Cixi lost control of Beijing after a short, but hard-fought campaign; she fled to Xi'an.
The Eight Banners were first developed by Nurhaci to organize Jurchen society beyond petty clan affiliations.
The Green Standard Army, made up of Ming troops who had surrendered to the Qing, eventually outnumbered Banner troops three to one.
The Canton System, established in 1756, restricted maritime trade to Canton and gave monopoly trading rights to private Chinese merchants.
The Sino-French War ended in 1885 with the Treaty of Tientsin (1885) and Chinese recognition of the French protectorate in Vietnam.
Xinjiang was established as a province in 1884, after the Qing court defeated Yaqub Beg, who had invaded with British support.

entities.name: Qing dynasty
entities.role: Last imperial dynasty of China, ruling from 1644 to 1912, also called the Great Qing or Manchu dynasty.

entities.name: Ming dynasty
entities.role: Dynasty that preceded the Qing and whose last ruler, the Chongzhen Emperor, committed suicide when Beijing fell.

entities.name: Zeng Guofan
entities.role: Chinese official who organized regional and village militias into the emergency army tuanlian and the Xiang Army.

entities.name: Li Hongzhang
entities.role: Colleague and mentee of Zeng Guofan who created the Huai Army, successor to the Xiang Army.

entities.name: Puyi
entities.role: Child emperor who abdicated in 1912 and was later installed as emperor of Manchukuo.

entities.name: Cixi
entities.role: Empress Dowager who participated in state affairs, declared war on the Eight-Nation Alliance, and died in 1908.

entities.name: Guangxu Emperor
entities.role: Qing emperor who died on November 14, 1908, reportedly poisoned with arsenic.

entities.name: Yuan Shikai
entities.role: General who was dismissed from power and later brought back to military power to crush the revolution.

entities.name: Li Zicheng
entities.role: Former minor Ming official who led rebels that sacked Beijing in April 1644 and established the short-lived Shun dynasty.

entities.name: Wu Sangui
entities.role: Ming general at Shanhai Pass who allied with the Manchus and was given the provinces of Yunnan and Guizhou.

entities.name: Dorgon
entities.role: Manchu prince who responded to Wu Sangui's appeal and insisted on making Beijing the dynastic capital.

entities.name: Nurhaci
entities.role: Founder who developed the Eight Banners and declared himself the Bright Khan of the Later Jin state.

entities.name: Hong Taiji
entities.role: Son of Nurhaci who expanded the banner system and renamed the dynasty Great Qing in 1636.

entities.name: Kangxi Emperor
entities.role: Qing emperor who welcomed Jesuit missionaries to his court and patronized the Kangxi Dictionary.

entities.name: Qianlong
entities.role: Qing emperor who propagated the image of himself as a Buddhist sage ruler and patron of Tibetan Buddhism.

entities.name: Sun Yat-sen
entities.role: Provisional head of the new Republic of China government established in Nanjing.

entities.name: Taiping Rebellion
entities.role: Rebellion during which Qing forces lost Nanjing in 1853 and Taiping forces reached the suburbs of Tianjin.

entities.name: Boxers
entities.role: Righteous and Harmonious Fists who murdered foreign missionaries and besieged the Foreign Legation Quarter in 1900.

entities.name: Eight-Nation Alliance
entities.role: Coalition of European, Japanese, and Russian armies that entered China in 1900 and took control of Beijing.

entities.name: Xiang Army
entities.role: Hybrid local militia and standing army raised in Hunan region under Zeng Guofan.

entities.name: Huai Army
entities.role: Successor to the Xiang Army, created by Li Hongzhang.

entities.name: Green Standard Army
entities.role: Ming troops who surrendered to the Qing and were used alongside Banner armies.

entities.name: Manchukuo
entities.role: State founded by the Empire of Japan in 1932 in Northeast China, with Puyi as emperor, which collapsed in 1945.

entities.name: Canton System
entities.role: 1756 policy restricting maritime trade to Canton and giving monopoly rights to private Chinese merchants.

entities.name: Sino-French War
entities.role: War that began with a French attack on the Chinese southern fleet at Fuzhou and ended in 1885 with the Treaty of Tientsin.

entities.name: Wuchang Uprising
entities.role: October 10, 1911 uprising that led to the creation of the Republic of China.

entities.name: Shanhai Pass
entities.role: Pivotal pass of the Great Wall located fifty miles northeast of Beijing.

entities.name: Xinjiang
entities.role: Region made a province in 1884 after the Qing defeated Yaqub Beg.
